canada.title: New powers announced for Moncton’s bylaw officers

canada.summary: If passed, the legislation would authorize police to access a businesses' registry of customers "when there are reasonable grounds to believe the information may assist in locating a victim of human trafficking."

canada.summary: Manitoba's CentrePort Canada is expanding and signed MOUs with Port of Churchill owner and global logistics company as the federal government analyzes where to spend $1 billion on four food terminals and 20-40 food hubs aimed at improving food security.

canada.title: N.L. seniors making $100K or less will get a cash payout in December: N.L. government

canada.title: ‘There’s been no failure,’ police chief says after Bridle Path home invasion suspect let go from hospital
canada.summary: On Monday, Toronto's police chief defended the decision not to arrest a 23-year-old suspect in an investigation into a violent home invasion last week who showed up at a hospital with a gunshot wound shortly after the incident.

canada.title: Committee urges more transparency in Yukon political fundraising, ban on foreign donations
canada.summary: The recommendations are included in an interim report recently released by the Yukon legislature's special committee on electoral financing. The committee was set up last spring to look at who can donate to the territory's political parties and how much they can give.

canada.title: Inside man or scapegoat? Defence, prosecutors make closing submissions in Pearson airport gold heist trial
canada.summary: Was a then-Air Canada employee an inside man who helped carry out one of the biggest gold heists in Canadian history, or a scapegoat exploited by a longtime friend? Those were the two competing scenarios presented to a Brampton, Ont., court Monday as prosecutors and defence lawyers made their closing submissions in the trial of Parmpal Sidhu.

canada.title: First Nations in B.C., environmental group call out foreign investment in liquid natural gas
canada.summary: An announcement that Mitsubishi Corporation will partner with Blackstone Credit & Insurance on the LNG Canada project in British Columbia, isn’t sitting well with some First Nations and an environmental group.

canada.title: Proposed data centre would release ‘23 Hiroshima-sized atomic bombs worth of energy’ a day, physicist says
canada.summary: An analysis of the mammoth Wonder Valley data centre suggests it would release the equivalent of 23 atom bombs of heat waste into the boreal forest of northwestern Alberta every day. A Utah State University physicist who conducted the review for the Sturgeon Lake Cree Nation said the project demands a full environmental impact assessment.
